approved_by: study owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3 (2026-10-06): revision-2 rule (aligned evidence is not automatically mandatory) approved; eight needs-review decisions and 14 flagged-item repairs applied; approval recorded after contract/rules/audit consistency and leak checks

functional_semantics.triton: field i decoded as ((b_uint8 & (3<<2i)) >> 2i).to(int8) - 1 paired with A columns i*K_b + j*BLOCK_K (impl_triton.py:72-77); int32 accumulation; int32 output.
functional_semantics.cutile: same decode ((B_int32 & mask) >> 2i) - 1 cast to int8, A block k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j (impl_cutile.py:56-66); int32 accumulation; int32 output.
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py:10-19 (host unpack to rows i*K_b + r, fp32 matmul with TF32 disabled, cast to int32, exact for the generated ranges). Generator tensors.py:439-448 returns int8 A and packed uint8 B; the config dtype label is ignored.

stages.note: Single-kernel blocked GEMM with grouped ordering and in-mainloop decode on both sides.

dependencies.triton: kernel depends on c and on bt (impl_triton.py:128,132/141).
dependencies.note: No intermediates besides the Triton-side bt (see preprocessing).

reduction_scan_sort.triton: outer loop over packed tiles j, inner static loop over fields i, int32 MMA accumulation (impl_triton.py:68-77).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: same j-outer / i-inner nesting with int32 MMA (impl_cutile.py:50-66).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same non-monotone logical-K visiting order; irrelevant for exact integer accumulation.

precision.triton: int8 x int8 -> int32 via tl.dot out_dtype=int32 (impl_triton.py:63,77); no float path.
precision.cutile: int8 x int8 -> int32 via ct.mma into an int32 accumulator (impl_cutile.py:46,66).
precision.note: Exact integer arithmetic on both sides; config.verify 0.1/0.1 is effectively exact for int32 outputs.

preprocessing.triton: bt = b.t().contiguous() (N, K_b) cached in a module-level WeakTensorKeyDictionary keyed by the B tensor object (impl_triton.py:16-24), looked up on every run (128): the transpose copy executes once per live B (warmup) and is untimed thereafter.
preprocessing.cutile: packed B consumed row-major as (TK, TN) tiles directly (impl_cutile.py:51-54); no cache, no transpose.
preprocessing.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the packed B is delivered row-major and no prepacked input may be assumed; consuming it directly (cuTile side) or through a K-major copy of the still-packed B rebuilt by device work inside every run() is a mapping choice, so the layout divergence is mapping-only. Any cross-call cache of a transformed operand is forbidden, so the manual Triton kernel's steady-state cached bt (impl_triton.py:16-24, 128) does not conform to the decided rule and its column is recorded as not comparable (human_reference_comparable = false); this is a reference-measurement caveat, not a contract ambiguity. Decoding stays inside the GEMM pass on both sides, as the contract requires.

intermediate_storage.triton: bt (N, K_b) uint8 retained for the lifetime of each B tensor (impl_triton.py:16-24).
intermediate_storage.cutile: none; widened B tile and decoded operand tiles are register resident (impl_cutile.py:55-65).
intermediate_storage.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): a per-call K-major copy of the packed B is a permitted, counted mapping-level intermediate; a copy that outlives the call via a cross-call cache is forbidden, and a globally materialised unpacked (K, N) B is forbidden outright. The Triton side's persistent bt is the non-conforming case covered by human_reference_comparable = false.

mutation.triton: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_triton.py:127).
mutation.cutile: a, b never written; fresh c per call (impl_cutile.py:82).
mutation.note: Idempotent. The reference sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False process-wide inside run() without restoring it (impl_torch.py:17).

hardware_dispatch.triton: no dispatch branches; K is a constexpr with static_assert K % (4*BLOCK_K) == 0 (impl_triton.py:40,46-49).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: no dispatch branches; K_b is ConstInt (impl_cutile.py:29); slab index k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j is only exact when K_b is a multiple of the K tile (57).
hardware_dispatch.note: Both sides are specialised per K and rely on tile-aligned K_b for the swept shapes (K = 1024*i); decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3) that only the declared shape is required and arbitrary K_b support is not. Descriptor-based vs tile loads are mapping details.

fq_boundary.note: The formula counts A once (int8), the packed B once (K*N/4 bytes) and C once (int32), with element sizes hard-coded. Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): it stays the declared lower-bound / compulsory-I/O model for scoring; the 2*K*N/4 bytes that a per-call K-major copy of the packed B adds are counted in the measured time but are diagnostic, not part of Q. Packed-byte reuse across fields is an optimisation and not modelled. The cuTile path matches the formula by reading the packed B directly and decoding in registers. The Triton path matches it in steady state only because the K-major copy runs once per live B and is cached in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary (impl_triton.py:16-24,128), never timed after warmup, which the decided rule forbids; the Triton column is therefore not comparable to contract-conforming implementations. The reference's host unpack and fp32 GEMM are reference-side work, not an F/Q issue.

review_items: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the K-major repack of the packed B, if an implementation uses one, is inside the timed algorithm: per call, uncached, rebuilt by device work inside every run(); no prepacked-input assumption. Decoding remains inside the multiplication path and a fully globally materialised unpacked (K, N) B is forbidden. The manual Triton timing excludes the repack (bt cached in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary, impl_triton.py:16-24,128), so the Triton column stays human_reference_not_comparable (human_reference_comparable = false); the cuTile column (direct (K_b, N) consumption, impl_cutile.py:51-54) is comparable. The open review item is removed from the contract (revision 2 retained).

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): only the benchmark's declared fixed shape is required (K a multiple of 1024 in every task); arbitrary K_b support is not required. The manual kernels' tile-aligned assumptions (static_assert K % (4*BLOCK_K) == 0, impl_triton.py:46-49; slab index k_a = i*num_tiles_kb + j, impl_cutile.py:57) are therefore within contract. The contract's requirement that any tail of the declared shape be masked (a zero-filled packed byte decodes to -1) is retained.

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the contract's earlier requirement that each packed byte be logically loaded exactly once per output tile is removed as contradictory with the free fields-inner / fields-outer loop order; packed-byte reuse is an implementation optimisation, not the canonical algorithm. Loop order is free so long as the packed B is decoded correctly inside the GEMM and no forbidden unpacked global intermediate is introduced.

Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3, applied by extension from the matmul_fp32_fp16_fp8 decision): process-wide precision/backend flags are evaluator state, not candidate-controlled state; the evaluator owns their isolation at verification time (impl_torch.py:17 sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False inside run() without restoring it, which the harness must contain). A candidate reading or changing them is flagged by evaluator_rules (suspicious here, since this operator's integer path has no precision class to alter).
